chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ajdafi, who said: I heard him (peace be upon him) say:
"Separate between the Adhan (call to prayer) and the Iqamah (second call) by sitting or by praying two Rak'ahs."

key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: Adhan: The first call to prayer announcing the time for salat.
key_terms.بِجُلُوسٍ: Bi-julusin: By sitting (taking a brief rest or pause).
key_terms.بِرَكْعَتَيْنِ: Bi-rak'atayni: By praying two units (Rak'atayn) of voluntary prayer.
key_terms.وَالْإِقَامَةِ: Al-Iqamah: The second call to prayer, recited immediately before the prayer begins.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended way to separate the Adhan and Iqamah before prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* prescribes a deliberate pause between the call to prayer and the commencement of the congregational prayer, either through sitting or performing two voluntary rak'at. This practice underscores the spiritual transition from the announcement to the act of worship, allowing worshippers to settle their hearts and minds before standing before Allah. It reflects the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) and mindfulness (khushu') in the performance of daily rituals.
